name: Venkata Ganji
headline: AI infrastructure. Platform engineering. Production ownership.
intro: AI infrastructure and platform engineer with 12 years building and operating production distributed systems. At Apple, I owned GPU Kubernetes platform engineering, model-onboarding tooling and Solr infrastructure within a shared enterprise AI platform. My work connects cloud architecture, hardware, deployment automation, performance engineering and production reliability—from building the foundation to observability, high availability and recovery.

cases.title: Enterprise GenAI, from ingestion to inference
cases.deck: GPU Kubernetes ownership, model-onboarding tooling, search performance and production reliability across an internal enterprise AI serving platform.
cases.summary: I owned GPU Kubernetes platform engineering, model-weight serving and onboarding tooling, Solr infrastructure and performance engineering, and Mac document-conversion infrastructure. I co-owned the wider enterprise AI platform with the team, including ingestion/inference GitOps onboarding and observability. Elasticsearch and Milvus were shared ownership.
metrics: Project embeddings across five Solr clusters in one region; at least 90% active
cases.problem: Enterprise teams needed a shared platform for document Q&A, enterprise chat, incident intelligence and coding-agent workflows. These experiences depended on more than a model endpoint: documents had to be ingested, transformed and indexed; retrieval had to remain responsive; and model deployments needed repeatable artifact and runtime configuration. Different workloads also placed different demands on CPU, storage and GPU capacity.
ownership: Owned GPU Kubernetes platform build, lifecycle, tooling, capacity planning and production operations on AWS EKS, including upgrades, patching and incident response. Operated NVIDIA V100, A10G, L40S and A100 infrastructure.

Operated NVIDIA GPU Operator, Karpenter and cluster networking across environments, including Calico/Cilium. Connected GPU workload placement and cluster lifecycle decisions to model-serving requirements.

Designed and built model-weight serving and onboarding tooling: Helm/Argo CD, vLLM, S3-to-FSx staging, checksum validation and read-only mounts. Worked with tensor parallelism, GPU memory sizing, context limits and LoRA configuration.

Owned Solr infrastructure, performance, IaC and lifecycle tooling at approximately 200-node, multi-region scale. Supported 15,000+ embedding collections across five clusters in one region; co-owned Elasticsearch and Milvus.

Developed Go model-checksum and Kafka topic/user resource-generation tools. Built a TypeScript CLI to validate GPU allocation, tensor parallelism, model paths, storage mounts and startup probes before deployment.

Operated DCGM GPU monitoring with Prometheus/Grafana and co-owned wider observability. Led investigations across deployment readiness, storage/PVC failures, networking, queues and p95/p99 latency; coordinated root-cause analysis and corrective actions.

Coordinated US/APAC engineers, guided migrations and mentored teammates. Worked directly with customer leaders on incoming workloads, capacity and service constraints; partnered with developers on application GitOps onboarding.
Owned Mac conversion infrastructure, IaC and tooling; productionized EC2 Mac conversion with application developers.
flow: Ingest enterprise knowledge
Connectors and upload services stage source objects through an S3-backed access layer. Parsing, chunking and embedding services turn content into retrievable representations.
Retrieve and orchestrate

Search/vector services access Solr and OpenSearch indexes. Orchestration and agent services assemble context and invoke models through a routing layer. Kafka supports platform events and configuration dependencies.
Serve models across two paths

Self-hosted models run on a separate GPU EKS environment; a provider gateway reaches Vertex AI/Gemini. The model tooling stages weights to FSx for Lustre, validates checksums and mounts weights read-only for serving.
Own the distributed foundation
SolrCloud runs on EC2/EBS with ZooKeeper. Ansible-driven CloudFormation, Terraform foundations and Python utilities support provisioning, runtime configuration and lifecycle operations.
decisions: Separate application and model infrastructure
The architecture separates the ingestion/inference services from GPU model hosting. This lets application and model deployments have distinct capacity and runtime configurations.
Make model artifacts part of deployment

Weight staging, integrity checks, shared volumes, health probes and runtime values are first-class deployment steps. Configuration covers precision, context limits, memory budgets, tensor parallelism and LoRA serving.
Treat retrieval as a systems problem
I worked across JVM/GC, OS settings, cache behavior, query patterns and indexes. The reported latency improvement is a vector-query result, not an LLM generation benchmark.
results: Supported 15,000+ project-embedding collections across five Solr clusters in one region, with at least 90% active; owned Solr infrastructure at approximately 200-node, multi-region scale.
Reduced vector-query latency from approximately 7.0 seconds to 1.9 seconds through JVM/GC, operating-system, cache, query and index tuning.
Migrated 200 Solr nodes to Graviton/ARM64 while preserving query throughput, reducing cost 19.8% ($266K+ annualized).

Production configurations specified 226 application-cluster workers across two AWS regions and 105 West-region document-processing replicas for parsing, chunking and PDF conversion. These are configured desired counts, not a live fleet inventory.

Delivered $500K+ in combined Solr and Mac infrastructure savings. Component rates: $266K+ annualized from Solr and approximately $16K/month from EC2 Mac document conversion. The combined figure is not stated as an annual total.
cases.operations: I followed production failures across model artifacts, serving workloads, Kubernetes, storage and network dependencies. When incomplete model staging blocked checksum validation and serving readiness, I restored validated artifacts and made successful staging and validation a deployment prerequisite. I also diagnosed embedding-service timeouts caused by worker conntrack exhaustion, addressing connection pooling, bounded concurrency and conntrack sizing. DCGM GPU telemetry, Prometheus/Grafana, PCAP and application latency helped connect infrastructure behavior to user impact.
cases.scope: Sanitized logical architecture, with personal and team ownership distinguished. Configured worker and replica counts describe desired configuration rather than a live fleet inventory. Model names describe platform serving scope, not training ownership. Latency figures refer to vector queries; no LLM throughput, TTFT or GPU-utilization improvement is claimed.

cases.title: A cyber data lake across hardware and software
cases.engagement: Cloudwick · Cyber Data Lake / Amorphic · Nov 2016–Dec 2018
cases.deck: Turning packets, flows and security events into a correlated data platform, with performance work from the network interface through distributed storage.
cases.summary: I owned the three-rack cyber data lake infrastructure end to end: hardware and network integration, operational tooling and performance tuning. I connected PCAP, NetFlow, application logs and firewall events to a correlated distributed-data platform.
metrics: PCAP, flow, app and firewall telemetry
cases.problem: Security data arrived in different shapes and at different rates: raw packet capture, NetFlow, application logs and firewall events. The engineering challenge was to collect those signals, move them into distributed processing and storage, and make them useful together. A packet-capture path also has different bottlenecks from a log pipeline, so testing needed to span NICs, disks, network fabrics, brokers and analytics services.
ownership: Implemented collection of PCAP, NetFlow, application logs and firewall events to support a correlated cyber data lake.
Owned Supermicro servers, high-throughput NICs, IXIA and ToR / supervisor-switch integration in the three-rack capture/replay environment; tuned 40 Gb/s capture technology.
Owned operational and performance tooling across capture, hardware and distributed data; engineered Corelight/IXIA integrations and operated Hadoop, Kafka, Spark, Solr, HBase and Elasticsearch.
Built Prometheus monitoring for collector agents and automated cloud/on-premises deployment using CloudFormation, Ansible, Jenkins, GitLab, Kickstart, Puppet and Python APIs.
flow: Capture and replay traffic

Mirrored traffic reaches a packet broker and capture systems. A replay path feeds security tools and provides a controlled test environment. The rack topology separates data transfer from server-management networking.
Collect logs and flows

Collector and aggregator processes feed Kafka before data lands in HDFS. The supplied test-bed drawing distinguishes functional and performance environments, including different storage and broker configurations.
Process and investigate

The broader product uses distributed storage, processing and search components. My work connects the source telemetry and platform operations; the overview groups those capabilities without asserting one identical route for every data type.
Package for deployment

Gateway designs separate lightweight and larger footprints, with collector, message, storage and management roles. Cloud integration and automated builds make those roles deployable across environments.
decisions: Separate functional tests from performance tests

A functionally correct collector can still be limited by disk, broker capacity or the capture path. The test environment made those dimensions visible instead of treating every failure as an application problem.
Keep capture and management paths distinct
The multi-rack design separates the data-transfer network from server-management access. Capture/replay and security integrations can be reasoned about independently from routine host operations.
Observe the collector as well as the cluster
Prometheus monitoring at the collector layer complements distributed-platform operations. This gives the team visibility before data reaches the search or analytics tier.
results: Delivered a three-rack environment for packet capture/replay and security-tool integration.
Deployed and tuned 40 Gb/s capture technology across hardware and software boundaries; this is a technology rating, not a measured sustained end-to-end ingestion result.
Integrated multiple telemetry families and automated deployment and operational monitoring for the product's distributed stack.
cases.operations: This work required following a performance symptom across system boundaries: capture hardware, network links, storage media, the aggregation process, Kafka and HDFS. The architecture set is useful for discussing how I isolate bottlenecks and make a complex platform repeatable to deploy and support.
cases.scope: The walkthrough diagrams are simplified redraws; low-resolution previews of the supplied originals are available separately. Gateway capacities and test configurations are not promoted to production benchmarks. The separate Amorphic cloud reference is dated June 2019 and credits a team author; it is included only as product context, not as evidence that I personally designed that entire later architecture. Telemetry here does not mean OpenTelemetry.
supporting: Data-transfer and management networks across a three-rack integration environment.

cases.title: Moving a document platform beyond Hadoop
cases.role: AWS Cloud Solutions Architect & Infrastructure Consultant
cases.deck: A migration that connected data movement, search modernization, application access and operational recovery.
cases.summary: I delivered solutions architecture, software engineering and production operations across a nearly four-year Freddie Mac engagement. I led three mission-critical migrations, designed the Hadoop/Solr-to-S3/search transition, and led Spark migration development through production cutover.
metrics: Mission-critical programs led in the engagement
cases.problem: The legacy platform combined document storage, distributed search and application dependencies. Moving its files alone would not produce a usable cloud platform: document names and mappings, search records, access paths and recovery procedures all had to make sense in the target environment. The architecture drawings expose that migration as a set of distinct transformations rather than a single copy operation.
ownership: Led three mission-critical migrations across distributed-data and live application systems during the engagement, coordinating architecture, automation, data movement, performance testing and production transition.
Designed and productionized a document-platform migration from Cloudera Hadoop/Solr to AWS Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, ELK and S3.
Led development of Spark migration jobs moving Solr data into Elasticsearch/ELK and HBase data into S3.
Built reusable IaC and operations automation; designed Databricks, AWS Glue, Talend and S3 ingestion frameworks and Python/Airflow workflows; supported performance testing and production transitions.
flow: Read the legacy representation
Documents reside in the Hadoop environment, including HAR archive representations in the supplied migration drawing. Search and HBase data have related but distinct migration paths.
Transform and transfer

The drawing compares extraction/transfer/rename stages, a custom Spark extraction-transfer-validation job, and a DistCp path followed by MapReduce naming/mapping work. These are migration approaches shown in the design, not a claim that every branch ran for every dataset.
Preserve names and validate
The naming/mapping stage is visible in the source design. Validation is part of the custom Spark approach. These stages connect successful transport to usable target objects.
Integrate the target platform
S3 and Elasticsearch/ELK become part of a larger cloud architecture with private proxy access, identity integration, infrastructure automation and cross-region recovery.
decisions: Separate transport from transformation
DistCp can address bulk transfer, while archive extraction and target naming/mapping require additional work. The design makes those responsibilities explicit.
Keep document and search migrations coordinated
S3 objects and search records serve different roles. The migration program covered both, so the target architecture could support application behavior as well as storage.
Include operations in the migration scope
Provisioning, performance testing, snapshots and recovery were part of the engineering work. A cloud cutover needed an operating model as well as a target diagram.
results: Delivered the document-platform cloud migration and led Spark-based data migration development.
Led three mission-critical migration programs across the broader client engagement.
Provided technical leadership for teams of approximately three to eight engineers, spanning architecture through production transition.
cases.operations: I built Python, Airflow, Ansible and shell automation for snapshots, migration and instance bootstrap. In the same client engagement, I also built and productionized a hybrid-cloud DR environment with approximately 15-minute RPO and 2-hour RTO. Those recovery figures belong to that DR environment, not a claim that every migration achieved those targets.
cases.scope: The HAR diagram presents alternatives. It does not by itself establish the selected route for every workload, total bytes migrated, zero downtime or a benchmark. The leadership and delivery claims come from my career record; the drawing explains the technical approach.
questions: How did archive extraction differ from bulk transfer?
How did naming and mapping affect application compatibility?
What made the platform operationally ready after migration?

cases.title: Cloud-native platforms, from foundations to recovery
cases.role: AWS Cloud Solutions Architect & Infrastructure Consultant
cases.deck: Building the cloud foundation and carrying it through automation, production operations, high availability and disaster recovery.
cases.summary: I designed and productionized cloud infrastructure for a document and search platform—from networking, identity and reusable IaC to workload integration, production operations and hybrid-cloud disaster recovery. I worked across architecture, software tooling and operations to make the platform deployable, observable and recoverable.
metrics: RPO for the delivered DR environment
RTO for the delivered DR environment
cases.problem: A legacy application had to reach cloud storage and search while continuing to work with enterprise identity and private connectivity. A successful architecture needed consistent infrastructure across environments, controlled credentials, predictable application paths and a recoverable second-region footprint.
ownership: Designed proxy, load-balancing and autoscaling infrastructure supporting the document platform's move to AWS.
Developed reusable Terraform, CloudFormation and Ansible provisioning/landing-zone workflows covering compute, search, networking, IAM, secrets, encryption and cross-region storage.
Designed federated authentication using PingFederate, Vault, AWS IAM/STS, ADFS and SAML across four environments; partnered with InfoSec on on-premises-to-S3 connectivity.
Built platform deployment and operations tooling and worked across observability, high availability and recovery as part of end-to-end cloud platform delivery.
Built and productionized a hybrid-cloud DR environment using cross-region replication, S3, Airflow, Python and Elasticsearch/ELK, delivered within six months.
flow: Connect applications privately
The proxy-farm drawing places application access behind hybrid connectivity and a load balancer, with autoscaled proxies in private subnets and an S3 endpoint.
Federate identity

The later authentication drawing shows a SAML assertion exchanged with IAM/STS for temporary credentials. The earlier state uses Kerberos, directory authentication and DNS forwarding to Hadoop services; those are distinct stages of the platform's evolution.
Provision dependencies consistently
The landing-zone drawing composes roles, security groups, object storage and KMS resources under an infrastructure boundary, with configuration references in Parameter Store.
Prepare for regional recovery

The recovery drawing separates primary data/search from replicated data and backup artifacts in another region, with restore/on-demand infrastructure. My operating work connected these components to recovery automation.
decisions: Bridge the legacy application boundary
The proxy tier provides an integration point between the existing application and cloud services. The design also spreads proxies across availability zones and uses autoscaling.
Treat identity as architecture
Directory integration, federation and temporary AWS credentials influence how applications reach the data plane. They were designed alongside network paths, not added as an afterthought.
Make recovery and IaC reinforce each other
Reusable provisioning defines the target resources; backup/replication provides recoverable state. The architecture distinguishes those responsibilities, including an on-demand recovery footprint.
results: Productionized hybrid-cloud DR with approximately 15-minute RPO and 2-hour RTO, delivered within six months.
Designed federated authentication across four environments and reusable infrastructure automation for cloud platform services.
Supported a mission-critical document/search platform through migration, operations and infrastructure performance testing.
cases.operations: My responsibility continued beyond provisioning. I connected cloud architecture with reusable Terraform, CloudFormation and Ansible workflows, bootstrap and operations automation, operational visibility, and recovery procedures. I worked across security requirements, application behavior and infrastructure dependencies, following the application request through proxy and identity paths and explaining how the platform could be provisioned and restored.
cases.scope: Drawings represent different releases and environments; the portfolio shows their relationship without implying that every identity mechanism runs in the same request path. Recovery metrics are career-reported results for the described DR environment, not a universal service guarantee.
supporting: Hybrid connectivity, load balancing, private-subnet proxies and S3 endpoint access.
Legacy directory authentication and later SAML/STS federation shown as separate paths.
Reusable infrastructure boundary composing identity, networking, storage, encryption and configuration.
questions: Why was the proxy tier useful during the migration?
How did federation change the credential flow?
How did infrastructure automation support disaster recovery?

kubernetes_story.title: The Kubernetes foundation behind AI serving.
kubernetes_story.intro: At Apple, I owned the GPU Kubernetes foundation on EKS: cluster build, lifecycle, tooling, capacity planning and production incidents. I also co-owned the application platform around it, partnering with developers on ingestion and inference GitOps onboarding.
cards: Owned GPU cluster build, upgrades, patching and operations across NVIDIA V100, A10G, L40S and A100 environments. Operated GPU Operator, Karpenter and cluster networking.
Personally built model-weight staging and checksum-validation tooling. Connected GPU allocation, tensor parallelism, storage mounts and startup readiness with deployment configuration.
Worked with customers on workload and capacity needs. Used DCGM, Prometheus/Grafana and application signals to investigate across GPU resources, networking, queues and persistent storage.
stages: Application services and GPU model hosting ran in separate Kubernetes environments. I owned GPU cluster build and lifecycle, while co-owning the wider application platform. Node upgrades and patching had to account for model reload time and serving availability.

I personally built model-onboarding tooling to stage weights from S3 to FSx, validate checksums and mount artifacts read-only. Helm/Argo CD delivered model workloads; Flux/Kustomize supported application GitOps onboarding.

I operated Karpenter and GPU Operator and planned capacity against model placement and customer workloads. Calico and Cilium appeared in different cluster generations; networking, DNS and storage had to be ready before a serving endpoint was useful.

DCGM GPU metrics, Prometheus/Grafana, network captures, p95/p99 latency and queue/storage signals supported investigation. I led production recovery and coordinated root-cause analysis and corrective actions.
stack: NVIDIA GPU Operator · Karpenter · managed node groups; KEDA, HPA and Prometheus Adapter supported workload-specific scaling.
Calico in older configurations; Cilium hybrid mode in newer environments. Wider platform components included AWS VPC CNI, NGINX ingress and Istio.
DCGM exporter · Prometheus Operator · Grafana · Kubernetes metrics and alerting · Splunk OpenTelemetry integration
cert-manager · Kubernetes RBAC · NetworkPolicy · FSx for Lustre model storage · PVCs and CSI integrations; Gatekeeper and EFS/EBS CSI appeared in wider platform configurations.
LeaderWorkerSet model-serving templates, Ray head/worker startup and KubeRay deployment configuration in adjacent infrastructure.
kubernetes_story.scope: I owned GPU platform engineering within a team-built AI platform. Tools varied by environment and cluster generation; this is a view of the operational ecosystem, not one identical installation everywhere.

inference_story.title: Production serving experience. Deeper inference engineering.
inference_story.intro: My foundation is hands-on production serving infrastructure. At Apple, I owned GPU Kubernetes engineering and personally built model-weight onboarding and serving tooling. I worked with vLLM runtime configuration, GPU memory sizing, tensor parallelism, context limits, LoRA and deployment readiness.
inference_story.learning: I’m now deepening my understanding of inference internals through structured study and practical exercises: prefill and decode, KV-cache behavior, scheduling, and reproducible latency and throughput measurement.
inference_story.contribution: I bring immediate ownership of serving-platform infrastructure, tooling, capacity planning and production troubleshooting. I am building on that experience to take on deeper inference-performance work, with the same habit of investigating across system boundaries.

cloud_native_story.title: From a blank cloud environment to a platform ready for production.
cloud_native_story.intro: I connect the full platform lifecycle: architecture, cloud foundations, infrastructure as code, workload deployment, observability, high availability and disaster recovery. My work at Freddie Mac and Apple combined design, hands-on engineering and ongoing production responsibility.
stages: Translate application needs into cloud architecture, networking, identity, compute and storage. Make infrastructure repeatable with Terraform, CloudFormation and Ansible.
Connect infrastructure to application delivery, Kubernetes and GitOps onboarding. Write deployment, bootstrap and lifecycle tooling to make delivery repeatable.
Build operational visibility through logs, metrics, dashboards and alerts. Investigate latency, network paths, queue backlogs and storage problems across the request and data flows.
Connect high availability with recoverable state, cross-region replication, backups and provisioning automation. Plan how the platform returns to service when a component or region fails.
evidence: Designed cloud foundations spanning private connectivity, load balancing, autoscaling, federated identity, storage and reusable IaC. Built and productionized hybrid-cloud disaster recovery with approximately 15-minute RPO and 2-hour RTO for that environment. My work covered architecture, tooling, observability and production operations.

Co-owned the enterprise AI platform with the team. Personally owned GPU Kubernetes build, lifecycle, tooling, capacity planning and production incidents, plus model-weight tooling, Solr infrastructure and Mac document-conversion infrastructure. Partnered with developers on application GitOps onboarding and observability.
